paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: what God claims, He claims for real. Back in Egypt, He struck down every firstborn in the land and set apart Israel's firstborn for Himself. Then He says, "The Levites belong to Me," and takes them in place of every firstborn Israelite (Numbers 3:12-13). Israel's firstborn were His, and the Levites stood in their place.

Now look at how careful He is. Every Levite gets counted, every firstborn gets counted, and when the numbers don't match, there's a redemption price of five shekels for each of the 273 extra (Numbers 3:46-47). Nobody gets lost in the math, and nobody is waved off as a rounding error. I think that's the heart of it, baker: when God says something is His, He doesn't say it loosely, and He sees every single one. I once bagged cookies by the handful, and God is NOT doing that.

The Levites teach us something else too. They didn't get the spotlight, since the priesthood stayed with Aaron and his sons, but their work was holy, from the curtains to the ark to the tent pegs (Numbers 3:25-37). Being set apart for God didn't always mean being up front. It meant being His and doing the job He gave you, and that matters whether yours is big or small. So whatever place you've been handed today, bring your whole self to it, because you belong to Him.
